message.content:
Here’s a quick list of well‑received documentaries you’ll want to check out if you’re interested in learning more about climate change:

| Title | Release Year | Synopsis |
|-------|--------------|----------|
| **“An Inconvenient Truth”** | 2006 | Former Vice President Al Gore presents an accessible overview of the science behind global warming, backed up by data visualizations and personal anecdotes. It sparked worldwide conversation and won two Oscars. |
| **“An Inconvenient Sequel: Truth to Power”** | 2017 | A follow‑up that examines how governments and corporations have responded—or failed—to the warnings presented in the first film. It includes new footage from the Paris Climate Accord negotiations. |
| **“Before the Flood”** | 2019 | Leonardo DiCaprio travels around the globe meeting scientists, activists, and local communities affected by rising seas and extreme weather events. The film blends travelogue style with hard‑hitting facts. |
| **“Climate Change – The Facts”** | 2020 | An animated short produced by NASA that distills complex climate science into clear visuals—great for viewers who prefer concise explanations. |
| **“Our Planet” (Season 1)** | 2019 | While primarily focused on biodiversity, this Netflix series highlights how species loss ties directly to climate shifts. Narrated by Sir David Attenborough, it offers stunning cinematography alongside ecological context. |

### Where to Watch

* **Amazon Prime Video:** *An Inconvenient Truth*, *Before the Flood*
* **Netflix:** *Our Planet* (and many other nature/climate titles)
* **Hulu / Disney+:** *An Inconvenient Sequel* often appears as part of their “Documentary” collections
* **PBS or National Geographic Channels:** Frequently air all of the above films during special programming blocks

Feel free to let me know which one interests you most—I can give you deeper background info, discuss key takeaways, or help locate a streaming link!
